root_cause: This is a recurring, previously documented flaky-test pattern (pattern eb0b94c864ee1a85, now seen 8 times since 2026-09-11) affecting ARM64 ACL-backed CPU functional tests. A ComparePerfCountersCPUTest-style assertion checks that the ACL primitive type selected at runtime (primType) matches the expected 'acl_f32' tag, but intermittently the executor falls back to an unexpected 'undef_f32' primitive, likely due to non-deterministic ACL kernel/primitive selection or a race in the ARM Compute Library executor cache under parallel test execution on ARM64 runners. The failing test (smoke_MaxPool_CPU_4D/PoolingLayerCPUTest) differs each time (previously AvgPool, FC, ConvertCPULayerTest, etc.) which further indicates a shared non-deterministic selection path rather than a bug specific to the PR's changed files (Histc op implementation, unrelated to CPU pooling/ACL primitive selection). The current PR (#39286) only adds a new Histc-17 op/reference and does not touch ACL primitive selection code, supporting that this failure is unrelated to the PR's own changes.
reproduction_steps: Run the ARM64 CPU functional test suite locally on an ARM64 host with the ACL backend enabled: `ov_cpu_func_tests --gtest_filter=*smoke_MaxPool_CPU_4D*PoolingLayerCPUTest*CompareWithRefs*acl*` repeatedly (several hundred iterations) under parallel load; the primType mismatch does not reproduce deterministically and may require running the full parallel suite (run_parallel.py with --workers 16) to trigger the race.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed CPU functional tests job; this is a known flaky pattern unrelated to the current PR's Histc changes.

Investigate ACL executor/primitive selection caching for thread-safety issues under parallel test execution (src/plugins/intel_cpu, ACL executor factory) to find why primType can resolve to 'undef' instead of the expected backend tag.
Consider adding a retry or quarantine marker for pooling/conversion tests exhibiting this primType flake on ARM64 ACL until the root cause in the ACL executor selection is fixed.
prevention_strategies: Add thread-safety assertions or tracing around ACL primitive/executor selection in the CPU plugin's ARM64 path, and track this specific flaky signature (eb0b94c864ee1a85) to prioritize a permanent fix once it crosses a higher recurrence threshold.
historical_context: This exact signature (primType is unexpected ... undef_f32 Expected ... acl_f32, category Flaky Test) has now recurred 8 times since 2026-09-11 across unrelated PRs (#39251, #39245, #38669, #38528, #38052, #37885, #37783, and now #39286), each time on a different smoke test (AvgPool, MaxPool, etc.), confirming it is an infrastructure-level ARM64/ACL flake rather than a code regression introduced by any single PR.
